reviews.text: A guarantee for our animal friends

Here I found understanding and compassion for my cancer dog... I found competence and availability in a very delicate situation. The staff is very kind and you can tell they work out of passion, not so much for business. I highly recommend them!

The staff was incredibly arrogant and rude! I came in to get my dog ​​vaccinated, and they treated me with unprecedented rudeness. Their manner was rude and lacked the slightest bit of kindness. It was clear they had no desire to work or pay attention to a customer who would have become loyal by having a puppy. Change jobs, you're scaring people away. Unbelievable!!

With my heart heavy with grief over the loss of my beloved cat, I feel compelled to write these words, not to honor a simple experience, but to give voice to a sense of injustice that has overshadowed our time of mourning. My cat was not just a pet, but a member of the family, a companion who filled our lives with love, affection, and small daily joys. Her death has left us with profound sorrow, but what has made this separation even more heartbreaking is the indifference with which we were treated at such a fragile and painful time. Alas, if only veterinarians understood that in their hands they hold not just bodies, but pieces of the hearts of entire families, perhaps, just perhaps, their profession could once again embody the sensitivity and respect it deserves. Unfortunately, in our experience, this has not happened, and so the decisions, so lightheartedly made, that were presented to us have inevitably led to a heartbreaking and, to say the least, shocking outcome. It's difficult to find the right words to express how frustrating and, at the same time, shocking it is to see how the most precious thing in our lives has been treated like a mere formality, a simple procedure to be completed. Every animal is a world unto itself, a unique entity deserving of respect and care, not only in body but also in soul. Yet, when a family member finds themselves in the hands of a doctor, the emotional and human aspect should never be forgotten.
Unfortunately, I cannot, and never will, assign the score this experience deserves—a more than deserved zero—but alas, that option is not an option. Words cannot do justice to the pain we feel, but I hope these words can serve to raise awareness among those responsible for treating lives, so that they never forget that behind every animal is a suffering family, a beating heart, and a part of us that breaks. To my sweet cat, who now rests in peace, goes my eternal memory and the affection that will never fade. Her presence, even if physically absent, will remain forever in our hearts. In closing, I hope this reflection goes to our dear veterinarians. When you choose a profession that saves lives, you must be beyond convinced. Study, stay up-to-date, and ensure that no other animal enters alive and leaves dead. Don't be superficial. Learn from my beloved cat, who still had a life of cuddles and love ahead of her. Finally, this goes to all the owners who would like to entrust themselves to this clinic. I say to you with all my heart: move on, find something else, and live your long life with your furry friends.

CLAUDIA PIA BADOLATO

The first time I took my Juke to the clinic, we were scared, misinformed, and full of doubts. The entire staff, from Monica to the doctors and Dr. Navas, reassured us, and in no time (the day before and the next day, having already had all the required tests and scans), my Juke was smiling again. Before this clinic, since it was August, we rushed from one vet to another before they all went on vacation, and the inhumanity shown by the other facilities disheartened us. Then, miraculously, we were recommended Clinica Veterinaria Vomero Vet, and peace returned. I also want to emphasize that even though costs are not considered in these cases (but many take advantage of them), we were extremely satisfied with this as well. I would recommend them to anyone for their professionalism, humanity, and reliability. Thank you from me and Juke.

One is the worst: they wanted to operate on him, I agreed to give him 45 days to schedule the date, the dog went on the bridge two days before the operation. He would have died anyway, but it wasn't possible to operate on him, or at least it wasn't necessary.
I wanted to thank Prof. Navas and his staff for operating on Diego for thyroid cancer. Great professionalism, thank you from Diego and all of us.
Dr. Navas, in addition to being competent and professional, has a humanity that is now rare.
I found competence, courtesy and great availability in the structure....I highly recommend it for our furry children.
Excellent and very kind doctor, a guarantee

The center is small but welcoming. The doctors are helpful, competent, and empathetic with the animals. The initial visit lasted over half an hour, and I received very helpful information, considering it was my first time there. Any tests are performed on the spot. I then called a few days later to ask for urgent clarification, and they contacted me again.
